title: Endoscopic submucosal and intermuscular dissection - German registry study
summary:
Precancerous lesions or early-stage cancers in the gastrointestinal tract can often be treated using a specialized endoscopic technique, without the need for surgery. During this procedure, abnormal tissue changes are removed layer by layer from the intestinal wall using an endoscope, while the affected section of the bowel is preserved. However, there is currently little data on how patients fare in the long term after these procedures.
This study aims to answer how patients develop over the long term following these minimally invasive procedures: How often does the disease recur? What complications can arise? The goal is to better assess the quality and safety of these procedures and to further develop treatment standards.
Data will be collected from patients who undergo one of the described procedures and who consent to participate. The medical treatment itself is not altered by participation in the study. In addition to information from the medical records, participants will be asked about their health status 1, 3, and 5 years after the procedure. The study will run for 7 years across multiple hospitals in Germany. All data will be stored confidentially and without direct identification of participants.

interventions.name:
This is a multicentre registry study collecting data generated in the course of routine clinical care. No control group is planned. Randomisation and blinding are not planned.
